<https://twitter.com/algo_luca|@algo_luca>: What project-driven books would you recommend in the software space?
Learning by building something non-trivial.

I have come across "Building Git" from @SCogLab, "Writing an Interpreter in Go" by @thorstenball.
What other good resources would you add to the list?
attachments.text:
What project-driven books would you recommend in the software space?
Learning by building something non-trivial.

I have come across "Building Git" from @SCogLab, "Writing an Interpreter in Go" by @thorstenball.
What other good resources would you add to the list?

attachments.fallback: <https://twitter.com/MustakimAli|@MustakimAli>: <https://twitter.com/algo_luca|@algo_luca> <https://twitter.com/SCogLab|@SCogLab> <https://twitter.com/thorstenball|@thorstenball> Not a book, it's a livestream of building a compiler from scratch <https://github.com/terrajobst/minsk/blob/master/README.md>

attachments.fallback: <https://twitter.com/danmunckton|@danmunckton>: <https://twitter.com/algo_luca|@algo_luca> <https://twitter.com/SCogLab|@SCogLab> <https://twitter.com/thorstenball|@thorstenball> You could skip the book and go directly to the software - choose some non-trivial open source project and clone a bit of it in another language (Rust of course). I’m doing this right now with Redis and I’m learning loads
